title: Repository and toolchain audit — intended behavior
statement: A new engineer can reproduce the selected baseline from recorded commands and lockfiles.

title: Repository and toolchain audit — safety/edge behavior
statement: Missing tools or external dependencies are reported as unavailable, never represented as tested.

title: Contract and fixture ownership — intended behavior
statement: Rust/TypeScript serialization uses the same IDs, revisions, decimal sequences, and error contract.

title: Contract and fixture ownership — safety/edge behavior
statement: A breaking payload or inconsistent generated OpenAPI fails the contract check.

title: GPUI bootstrap and native package pin — intended behavior
statement: The selected GPUI release, compiler, and native SDK produce a reproducible windowed release build.

title: GPUI bootstrap and native package pin — safety/edge behavior
statement: Current-main and published-crate API differences cannot be silently mixed.

title: Composer, IME, and accessibility risk spike — intended behavior
statement: IME composition, selection, clipboard, undo, and keyboard/screen-reader traversal work on the chosen matrix.

title: Composer, IME, and accessibility risk spike — safety/edge behavior
statement: Enter during active IME composition never sends a message or loses input.

title: SQLite cache, drafts, and migrations — intended behavior
statement: Drafts and message/search projections survive process restart and migrate without loss.

title: SQLite cache, drafts, and migrations — safety/edge behavior
statement: Account/workspace mixing, failed transactions, and revoked-content search leakage are rejected.

title: Threat model and authority boundaries — intended behavior
statement: Every privileged surface has an owner, threat model, policy source, and negative test plan.

title: Threat model and authority boundaries — safety/edge behavior
statement: A separate but unrestricted process is not accepted as a sandbox.

title: Verified identity, tenancy, and memberships — intended behavior
statement: An authenticated human sees and mutates only permitted workspace resources across clients.

title: Verified identity, tenancy, and memberships — safety/edge behavior
statement: Cross-tenant IDs, revoked sessions, and forged actor/role fields cannot disclose or modify data.

title: Effect service runtime and typed errors — intended behavior
statement: Startup validates configuration and services expose typed failures with scoped resource cleanup.

title: Effect service runtime and typed errors — safety/edge behavior
statement: Missing secrets, interrupted work, and malformed requests fail closed without content leakage.

title: Native timeline and pending sends — intended behavior
statement: Cached navigation and durable local sends work while the agent engine is stopped.

title: Native timeline and pending sends — safety/edge behavior
statement: Slow network, oversized content, variable row heights, and failed sends do not freeze input or discard drafts.

title: Shared messaging transaction and outbox — intended behavior
statement: One operation produces one accepted message/revision and one consistent event history.

title: Shared messaging transaction and outbox — safety/edge behavior
statement: Lost responses, duplicate requests, changed idempotency payloads, and concurrent edits do not duplicate or overwrite work.

title: Resumable selective synchronization — intended behavior
statement: Reconnect converges messages, read state, and pending intent without losing local drafts.

title: Resumable selective synchronization — safety/edge behavior
statement: Expired cursors, revoked membership, late commits, duplicates, and tombstones cannot leak or resurrect content.

title: Task and versioned work-contract model — intended behavior
statement: A message becomes a bounded task with a human-confirmed current contract.

title: Task and versioned work-contract model — safety/edge behavior
statement: Changing acceptance criteria or authority cannot mutate an already-bound contract invisibly.

title: Authoritative policy and dispatch guards — intended behavior
statement: Current owner, agent, source, action, environment, audience, and policy permissions intersect before dispatch.

title: Authoritative policy and dispatch guards — safety/edge behavior
statement: Client-supplied approval flags or permission facts never become trusted authority.

title: Durable coordinator baseline and replay — intended behavior
statement: Run state survives worker restarts and durable approval waits with one current coordinator.

title: Durable coordinator baseline and replay — safety/edge behavior
statement: History replay, worker upgrade, and duplicate delivery cannot create a second authoritative run.

title: Deterministic simulated agent — intended behavior
statement: The simulator produces stable artifacts/evidence through the real task/run interfaces.

title: Deterministic simulated agent — safety/edge behavior
statement: Simulation is visible and cannot accept credentials or perform actual external actions.

title: Native workroom and progress cards — intended behavior
statement: A teammate can see outcome, owner, environment, state, blockers, and artifacts without opening a terminal.

title: Native workroom and progress cards — safety/edge behavior
statement: High-volume activity never floods the human timeline or steals scroll/focus.

title: Protected artifact upload and versions — intended behavior
statement: Permitted users can inspect exact versioned artifacts and protected derivatives.

title: Protected artifact upload and versions — safety/edge behavior
statement: Incomplete, oversized, wrong-digest, cross-task, and unauthorized uploads do not become accepted artifacts.

title: Version-bound review and acceptance — intended behavior
statement: Acceptance names exact contract/artifact versions and preserves historical decisions.

title: Version-bound review and acceptance — safety/edge behavior
statement: Agent success, stale artifact versions, or unauthorized reviewers cannot auto-accept work.

title: Authenticated browser reviewer — intended behavior
statement: A second person reviews work without installing the desktop app or relying on the initiator being online.

title: Authenticated browser reviewer — safety/edge behavior
statement: Forwarded/expired/revoked links and changed approval bindings cannot broaden access.

title: First complete two-human vertical slice — intended behavior
statement: Two users complete the flow without narrated assistance or manual database edits.

title: First complete two-human vertical slice — safety/edge behavior
statement: Offline/restart, failed-check, and changed-artifact variations remain clear and safe.

title: Authenticated broker capability protocol — intended behavior
statement: Every tool request is bound to run generation, permitted resources, expiry, and action intent.

title: Authenticated broker capability protocol — safety/edge behavior
statement: Guessing a socket path, replaying a grant, or forging a session frame cannot execute a tool.

title: Local sandbox and process enforcement — intended behavior
statement: A disposable local run executes permitted commands without host-wide authority.

title: Local sandbox and process enforcement — safety/edge behavior
statement: Symlink traversal, malicious repository scripts, secret inheritance, and broker bypass attempts are contained.

title: Connector credentials and installation — intended behavior
statement: Users can install the least-privilege integration required for one project and see data destinations.

title: Connector credentials and installation — safety/edge behavior
statement: Token expiry, webhook replay, revoked scopes, and unintended token audiences fail safely.

title: First real coding-agent adapter — intended behavior
statement: The real adapter produces bounded changes/artifacts through the same task/run contract.

title: First real coding-agent adapter — safety/edge behavior
statement: Unsupported capabilities, malformed tool output, and requested privilege expansion are explicit and denied by default.

title: Transactional action intents and approvals — intended behavior
statement: A valid current decision authorizes one specific publication/action with a stable operation ID.

title: Transactional action intents and approvals — safety/edge behavior
statement: Concurrent consumption, replay, changed destination/artifact, and uncertain provider results cannot duplicate or broaden effects.

title: Usage reservations and spending limits — intended behavior
statement: Budget checks reserve before dispatch and reconcile actual usage, including failed attempts.

title: Usage reservations and spending limits — safety/edge behavior
statement: Concurrent reservations, duplicate settlements, and estimate overruns cannot hide spend or continue unlimited work.

title: Cancellation and process lifecycle — intended behavior
statement: Users can stop new work and understand which in-flight operations are still reconciling.

title: Cancellation and process lifecycle — safety/edge behavior
statement: A provider timeout or process signal does not falsely report already-completed external effects as undone.

title: Isolated hosted execution runner — intended behavior
statement: Shared work can continue independently of a laptop under one durable coordinator.

title: Isolated hosted execution runner — safety/edge behavior
statement: Host sockets, cloud metadata, broad credentials, and noisy-neighbor resource escapes are unavailable.

title: Checkpoint handoff and generation fencing — intended behavior
statement: Supported work resumes locally/cloud-side from a known checkpoint with resolved destination credentials.

title: Checkpoint handoff and generation fencing — safety/edge behavior
statement: Delayed old-runner output and unresolved external actions cannot create split authority or blind retries.

title: Inspectable context and source permissions — intended behavior
statement: Users inspect/correct the sources a run uses and their model/output destinations.

title: Inspectable context and source permissions — safety/edge behavior
statement: Private source summaries, stale ACLs, and hidden source titles cannot leak into broader audiences.

title: Local and server permission-aware search — intended behavior
statement: Authorized cached results arrive promptly and server results extend them without disrupting selection.

title: Local and server permission-aware search — safety/edge behavior
statement: Revoked/deleted content, autocomplete, result counts, and cross-account caches do not reveal private sources.

title: Decision-focused inbox and notifications — intended behavior
statement: Users can identify what needs action and still access chronological/unfiltered activity.

title: Decision-focused inbox and notifications — safety/edge behavior
statement: Repeated agent updates, reconnects, and muted channels do not create notification floods.

title: Adapter and model-destination conformance — intended behavior
statement: Supported adapters declare and pass their actual read/write/cancel/checkpoint/reporting capabilities.

title: Adapter and model-destination conformance — safety/edge behavior
statement: An unsupported provider capability or unapproved model destination cannot silently fall back to broader behavior.

title: Isolated generated previews — intended behavior
statement: Permitted reviewers inspect a generated preview without exposing privileged application interfaces.

title: Isolated generated previews — safety/edge behavior
statement: Preview scripts cannot access broker routes, app cookies, arbitrary local ports, or forbidden network destinations.

title: Cross-component observability and safe diagnostics — intended behavior
statement: Operators trace a run/action and identify queues, costs, failures, and recovery state.

title: Cross-component observability and safe diagnostics — safety/edge behavior
statement: Default logs/telemetry never include raw prompts, source text, credentials, or sensitive URLs.

title: Native and system performance regression suite — intended behavior
statement: Launch, cached switch/search, input, and concurrent streams are measured against declared budgets.

title: Native and system performance regression suite — safety/edge behavior
statement: Idle redraw loops, unbounded caches, log floods, and background work cannot hide behind average latency.

title: Native media risk spike — intended behavior
statement: A reproducible test demonstrates basic native media capture/render/lifecycle on the first platform.

title: Native media risk spike — safety/edge behavior
statement: SDK availability alone is not accepted as proof of screen-sharing or accessibility support.

title: Calls and audio collaboration — intended behavior
statement: Native/browser participants maintain usable audio with clear device/capture state.

title: Calls and audio collaboration — safety/edge behavior
statement: Device changes, sleep, network loss, and permission revocation do not leave hidden capture active.

title: Screen sharing and media privacy — intended behavior
statement: Users know what is shared and can reliably stop it across the supported platform matrix.

title: Screen sharing and media privacy — safety/edge behavior
statement: Recording/transcription remains off without implemented consent, access, and retention controls.

title: Signed desktop updates and rollback — intended behavior
statement: A client upgrades reproducibly while preserving drafts and compatible cache data.

title: Signed desktop updates and rollback — safety/edge behavior
statement: Unsigned/corrupt updates and interrupted migrations do not execute or destroy user work.

title: Windows compatibility and native acceptance — intended behavior
statement: Published Windows support matches actual recorded build and behavior evidence.

title: Windows compatibility and native acceptance — safety/edge behavior
statement: Framework source support is not substituted for tested end-user workflows.

title: Linux compatibility and native acceptance — intended behavior
statement: Published Linux support names tested distributions/backends and known limitations.

title: Linux compatibility and native acceptance — safety/edge behavior
statement: Untested compositor/assistive-technology behavior is not presented as supported parity.

title: Staged migration and structured export — intended behavior
statement: Authorized content imports/export reproducibly with provenance and explicit omissions.

title: Staged migration and structured export — safety/edge behavior
statement: Private channels, inaccessible files, repeated pages, and malformed identities cannot silently leak or duplicate.

title: Narrow Slack coexistence bridge — intended behavior
statement: Teams can evaluate one project without moving all daily communication.

title: Narrow Slack coexistence bridge — safety/edge behavior
statement: Mirrored edits/deletes, retries, and source revocation do not create loops or broaden access.

title: Saved items, reminders, and scheduled sends — intended behavior
statement: Users can save work and schedule permitted messages/reminders across devices.

title: Saved items, reminders, and scheduled sends — safety/edge behavior
statement: Revoked access, DST changes, duplicate scheduling, and stale permissions cannot send unauthorized messages.

title: Profiles, status, and notification preferences — intended behavior
statement: Ordinary team communication preferences work predictably across clients.

title: Profiles, status, and notification preferences — safety/edge behavior
statement: Muted/private content does not leak in push previews or cross-account notification routing.

title: Mobile messaging and safe review participation — intended behavior
statement: A teammate can participate in critical communication/review without the desktop app.

title: Mobile messaging and safe review participation — safety/edge behavior
statement: A small screen cannot obscure important approval details or allow stale/revoked decisions.

title: Daily communication edge-case completeness — intended behavior
statement: Target teams complete ordinary daily chat workflows with consistent semantics.

title: Daily communication edge-case completeness — safety/edge behavior
statement: Deleted thread roots, group membership changes, long content, and concurrent edits preserve privacy and user intent.

title: Collaborative documents — intended behavior
statement: Concurrent document editing converges without mixing document content with approval authority.

title: Collaborative documents — safety/edge behavior
statement: Offline merges cannot grant permissions, mutate accepted evidence versions, or bypass deletion policy.

title: Lightweight lists and work views — intended behavior
statement: Teams organize work with shared task identity and current permissions.

title: Lightweight lists and work views — safety/edge behavior
statement: View-specific edits cannot diverge from task state or expose hidden tasks.

title: Versioned reusable workflow recipes — intended behavior
statement: An installed recipe revalidates input, policy, budget, and approvals on every run.

title: Versioned reusable workflow recipes — safety/edge behavior
statement: Recipe updates and schedules cannot auto-grant new tools or continue under revoked ownership.

title: Guests and externally shared spaces — intended behavior
statement: Permitted outside reviewers collaborate without obtaining general workspace access.

title: Guests and externally shared spaces — safety/edge behavior
statement: Joining a group or forwarding a link cannot reveal previously private history by accident.

title: Enterprise SSO integration — intended behavior
statement: Organization identity policy applies across native/browser/mobile sessions.

title: Enterprise SSO integration — safety/edge behavior
statement: Misconfigured issuer/audience, account linking, and admin role changes do not widen access.

title: Provisioning and deprovisioning — intended behavior
statement: Removing a user stops future authority and identifies agents/workflows requiring reassignment.

title: Provisioning and deprovisioning — safety/edge behavior
statement: Out-of-order provisioning and stale sessions cannot resurrect revoked access.

title: Retention, holds, and deletion propagation — intended behavior
statement: Deletion affects permitted stores, indexes, derivatives, and export rules with documented limitations.

title: Retention, holds, and deletion propagation — safety/edge behavior
statement: Immutable logs, offline devices, and backups are not falsely represented as instantly purged.

title: Audit exports and privileged support access — intended behavior
statement: Admins can investigate authorized events without default access to every private message.

title: Audit exports and privileged support access — safety/edge behavior
statement: Support tools or exports cannot bypass resource policy or leak secrets/source text.

title: Company-managed runners — intended behavior
statement: Customer infrastructure executes bounded shared work with clear data/model destinations.

title: Company-managed runners — safety/edge behavior
statement: A local runner is not marketed as full self-hosting or allowed to create its own shared authority.

title: Enterprise execution-policy console — intended behavior
statement: Admins understand and change enforced execution policy with safe preview and rollout.

title: Enterprise execution-policy console — safety/edge behavior
statement: Policy edits cannot silently preserve stale approvals or leave forbidden work running unchecked.

title: Regional data placement and restore strategy — intended behavior
statement: Claims match databases, artifacts, workflow histories, backups, telemetry, and model routing.

title: Regional data placement and restore strategy — safety/edge behavior
statement: Single-region labels cannot hide cross-region or external-provider transfers.

title: Public SDK and webhook platform — intended behavior
statement: Third parties build safe task/artifact/approval integrations using stable contracts.

title: Public SDK and webhook platform — safety/edge behavior
statement: API clients have no privileged back door around the same human/agent permissions.

title: Reviewed integration marketplace — intended behavior
statement: Installed extensions disclose and stay within their permitted execution/data scope.

title: Reviewed integration marketplace — safety/edge behavior
statement: Popularity or connector text cannot substitute for executable-code review and isolation.

title: Bounded multi-agent delegation — intended behavior
statement: Parallel work improves accepted outcomes after accounting for review and cost.

title: Bounded multi-agent delegation — safety/edge behavior
statement: Recursive delegation and shared working-copy mutations cannot escape authority or budget limits.

title: Privacy-aware activation and outcome analytics — intended behavior
statement: Teams can measure activation, retention, review effort, rework, and cost consistently.

title: Privacy-aware activation and outcome analytics — safety/edge behavior
statement: Task splitting, failed-run exclusion, or content-bearing telemetry cannot inflate or leak metrics.

title: Transparent usage and pricing experiment — intended behavior
statement: Customers understand human collaboration charges versus execution usage and estimates.

title: Transparent usage and pricing experiment — safety/edge behavior
statement: Provider overages, duplicate charges, and failed attempts are not hidden from accounting.

title: Design-partner onboarding and paid pilots — intended behavior
statement: Teams repeatedly return without founder narration and identify measurable useful outcomes.

title: Design-partner onboarding and paid pilots — safety/edge behavior
statement: Demo praise alone is not treated as retention or willingness to switch.

title: Backup, restore, and disaster rehearsal — intended behavior
statement: Recovery objectives are supported by actual restore evidence and owner approval.

title: Backup, restore, and disaster rehearsal — safety/edge behavior
statement: Restored old workers and leases cannot resume as current owners without reconciliation.

title: Independent execution security review — intended behavior
statement: Critical authorization, isolation, update, and publication controls have independent evidence.

title: Independent execution security review — safety/edge behavior
statement: Unexecuted tests, reference functions, or simulated paths cannot be marked as production security coverage.

title: Replacement release candidate — intended behavior
statement: Target teams can conduct daily work without critical prior-workspace blockers.

title: Replacement release candidate — safety/edge behavior
statement: Marketing does not claim unsupported platforms, full parity, or certifications without evidence.

title: Distribution license and dependency audit — intended behavior
statement: Every redistributed component and executable dependency has recorded provenance and permitted use.

title: Distribution license and dependency audit — safety/edge behavior
statement: One framework license is not generalized to unrelated repository code or bundled assets.

title: Communication replacement gap audit — intended behavior
statement: Each supported parity claim names tested behavior, plan/platform scope, and evidence.

title: Communication replacement gap audit — safety/edge behavior
statement: A candidate inventory or webhook endpoint is not presented as exhaustive Slack equivalence.

title: Independent end-to-end acceptance — intended behavior
statement: A non-initiator confidently reviews current artifacts and understands evidence/limitations.

title: Independent end-to-end acceptance — safety/edge behavior
statement: A narrated founder demo or manually edited backend is not accepted as a working product flow.

title: Leadership benchmark and expansion decision — intended behavior
statement: Expansion decisions are supported by measured user value and clear economics.

title: Leadership benchmark and expansion decision — safety/edge behavior
statement: Feature count, native rendering, or agent activity alone is not treated as industry leadership.
